citations.claim: after one step energy jumps to ~2445 J, the first energy_bound violation
free-falling body accelerates from -60 to -66 in one dt=1/30 step (delta 6 instead of expected g*dt=1)

counterfactual.change: changed only gravity 30 -> 0; free-fall energy gain disappears and no rule is violated

explanation: Single body in free fall (no walls/contacts, controller off) gains ~315 J in one dt=1/30 step while gravity work for the ~2.1 m drop should be only ~63 J. The trace used 71 substeps; vy went from -60 to -66 (delta 6) instead of the expected g*dt=1, so the gravity velocity update is over-applied when high speed triggers substep splitting, directly producing the energy_bound violation.
vision_note: The single blue ball falls roughly two meters between step 0 and step 1 with slight rightward drift. No wall, collision, or controller influence is visible, so it looks like plain free fall in one large dt step.
